title: Potato and Cheese Dumplings with Buttery Golden Onions
summary: Soft sour-cream dough is wrapped around a creamy potato, farmer's cheese and golden onion filling, boiled until tender and then fried in butter until spotted gold, served with sour cream and chives.
equipment: 7.5 cm round cutter or a glass
2 trays and a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
cold water (up to 4 tbsp if needed)
floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper or russet), peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
medium onions, halved and thinly sliced
farmer's cheese (twaróg) or well-drained cottage cheese
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour and dough salt in the large bowl, add the egg and mix with a fork until clumpy. Work in the sour cream and soft butter with your fingertips to a rough, slightly sticky ball, adding the water 1 tbsp at a time only if dry flour remains. Knead for 3-4 min on a lightly floured surface until smooth and soft, then wrap and rest for 30 min at room temperature (or up to 24 h in the fridge, bringing it back to room temperature for 20 min before rolling). Resting relaxes the gluten, so the dough rolls thin without springing back.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.text: Melt the 30 g filling butter in the frying pan over medium heat, add the onions and cook for 15-20 min, stirring often, until soft and deep golden. Turn the heat down if they brown too quickly. Slow cooking draws out their natural sugars for a sweet, rich flavour.

steps.title: Boil and mash the potatoes
steps.text: Put the potatoes in the saucepan, cover with cold unsalted water by 2-3 cm and bring to the boil. Simmer for 12-15 min until a knife slides in with no resistance, then drain well and leave to steam dry in the colander for 2 min. Rice or mash them smoothly while hot; hot potato cells break apart cleanly, giving a smooth rather than gluey mash.

steps.title: Finish the filling
steps.text: Stir in the cheeses, filling salt, pepper and half the onions, keeping the rest for serving. Spread the mixture on a plate and cool completely, about 30 min. Warm filling softens the dough and makes it tear.

steps.title: Roll and fill
steps.text: Cut the dough in half, keeping one half wrapped, and roll the other on a lightly floured surface to 2 mm thick. Cut 7.5 cm rounds, place a heaped tablespoon (about 17 g) of filling in the centre of each, fold into a half-moon and pinch the edges firmly from one end to the other, pressing out any air; crimp with a fork if you like. Trapped air expands in the boiling water and can burst the seams.

steps.title: Repeat and reroll
steps.text: Set the pierogi on a floured tray in a single layer under a tea towel. Gather the scraps, rest them for 5 min and reroll once, then repeat with the second half of dough. You should end up with about 40, using up all the filling.

steps.title: Boil in batches
steps.text: Bring a large pan of unsalted water to a rolling boil and lower in 10-12 pierogi at a time, stirring gently once so none stick. Once they float, cook for 2-3 min more until the dough edges are tender; cut into one to check the edge is soft, not chewy. Lift out with the slotted spoon onto a tray in a single layer.

steps.title: Fry and serve
steps.text: Reheat the reserved onions with the 20 g serving butter in the frying pan over medium heat. Add the pierogi in batches and fry for 2-3 min per side until golden in spots. Serve hot, about 10 per person, topped with the onions, with sour cream and chives.

tips: A common mistake is filling the dough while the potato mixture is still warm; let it cool completely so the wrappers do not tear.
Pinch the edges firmly and press out all the air, or the pierogi may split as they boil.
Do not overcrowd the pan when boiling; 10-12 at a time keeps the water at a rolling boil.
Keep the dough you are not rolling wrapped so it does not dry out and crack.
storage: Cool within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat by pan-frying in a little butter until piping hot (74°C). Freeze uncooked pierogi on a tray, then bag them, for up to 3 months; boil from frozen, adding 2-3 min.
